attribution: Mike Jensen — CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Snow-covered peaks and red fishermen's cabins around Reine at blue hour.
caption: Reine on Moskenesøya in winter blue hour, the base for two nights in a traditional rorbu. Snow on the peaks is why the Reinebringen climb is replaced by guided snowshoeing and coastal walks on this trip.

attribution: Giuseppe Milo from Dublin, Ireland — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Hamnøy fishing village on the Lofoten coast in late-winter light, photographed in February.
caption: Hamnøy, a few minutes' drive from Reine on the E10, photographed in February. The rorbuer here were built for the winter cod fishery that still defines Lofoten's calendar.

commonsFile: File:Drying Stockfish at Henningsvær, Lofoten, Norway.jpg
attribution: Christoph Strässler — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Wooden racks of cod drying in the open air at Henningsvær.
caption: Skrei cod hung to dry as stockfish at Henningsvær. The racks fill between roughly February and April, so a March visit sees the working fishery rather than a museum version of it.

commonsFile: File:Drying codfish heads hanging in Å i Lofoten, Moskenesøya, Lofoten, Norway, 2015 April - 2.jpg
attribution: Ximonic (Simo Räsänen) — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Rows of cod heads hanging on drying racks in Å at the end of the E10.
caption: Cod heads drying at Å, where the E10 ends and the Norwegian Stockfish Museum sits in the old fishing station. The heads are exported for food, a reminder that this coast's economy is still the sea.

commonsFile: File:Oksneset and Ersfjorden from Tungeneset in low sunlight, Senja, 2012 October - 2.jpg
attribution: Ximonic (Simo Räsänen) — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Okshornan mountains and Ersfjorden seen in low sunlight from the Tungeneset viewpoint on Senja.
caption: Tungeneset viewpoint on Senja's National Tourist Route, shown here in October low sun. In March the same road runs through snow, and the viewpoint is a short walk from the car.

attribution: Bheem Adavikolanu — CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Snow-covered houses and harbour of Tromsø in late March light.
caption: Tromsø in late March, with snow still deep on the island city. The group bases itself here for two nights for dog-sledding, a Sámi-led reindeer visit and an aurora chase.

attribution: Andi Gentsch — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Green northern lights over the Tromsø area.
caption: Northern lights over Tromsø. Mid-March is close to the equinox peak in geomagnetic activity, but clear skies matter more than any month, so the itinerary has two nights in Tromsø and flexible evenings elsewhere.

attribution: Lorie Shaull — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A Sámi woman feeding a reindeer near Tromsø.
caption: A Sámi herder feeding a reindeer near Tromsø. The trip pairs this kind of visit with Kautokeino, so the encounter is with people who live from reindeer herding, booked through Sámi-owned operators.

attribution: DXR — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The titanium-clad Northern Lights Cathedral in Alta.
caption: The Northern Lights Cathedral (Nordlyskatedralen) in Alta, a church built in 2013 with a spiralling titanium facade. It is an evening stop in Alta on day 10 before the group's drive to Kautokeino.

attribution: Heidi Johansen — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Prehistoric rock carvings at Bergbukten in the Rock Art of Alta UNESCO site.
caption: Rock carvings at Bergbukten, part of the Rock Art of Alta UNESCO World Heritage Site, shown in summer. In March the outdoor trail is under snow, so the group sees the carvings at the Alta Museum's indoor exhibition.

attribution: Lars Engerengen — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Wooden church in Kautokeino in March with snow on the ground.
caption: Kautokeino church in March. Kautokeino is the centre of Sámi reindeer herding in Norway and hosts the Easter festival, with reindeer racing and the Sámi Grand Prix, each spring.

attribution: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Rombaken fjord and the town of Narvik seen from above.
caption: Narvik on the Rombaksfjord, the first night. The 1940 naval battles fought here are told in Narvik's war museum, which opens the trip's history thread after the evening arrival.
